status: resolved locally; not committed or published
method: Codex reread all 537 unique base sentences and their 1500 blanks, reconciled the prior 40 flags, checked each of 60 omission candidates and 12 related alternatives in its unchanged full sentence, and checked all exact duplicate typed prompts/cues for answer-list consistency. Claude independently adjudicated the original 344-row patch, all 60 candidates and the 12 related alternatives (in nine groups). Definitions are evidence for senses, not proof of sentence equivalence. No exhaustive synonym or native-speaker certification is claimed.

keep with collocation caveat; not limited to crimes or accidents. DLE general sense and Fundéu's description of an organized evento as a programmed suceso refute the categorical rejection.

keep with construction caveat; an inanimate subject can prevent an implicitly human action. The familiar can't-help reading is not the only grammatical reading. Ministry of Health primary usage of an electronic prescription preventing visits supplies a counterexample to the asserted subject-control restriction.
keep; mere and uncomplicated readings are possible. Do not reject solely because one reading differs.
keep; wanting and affection readings coexist. DLE explicitly permits affection toward things.

baseSentenceFlags.reason: Aumentar permits a nonprepositional measure complement. The claim that en is obligatory was unsupported.

Impedir/evitar can take an infinitive with an implicit human subject. English us makes that understood participant explicit. This is marked wording, not an established error. The Ministry example supports the construction, not every possible collocation.
Fin can denote the endpoint of a process; al fin del proceso is not automatically the idiom al fin meaning finally. Final and término are also accepted.
